content_en: Unlike traditional managers, agile leaders:
option_1_content_en: Enable team members to act
option_2_content_en: Solve problems for the team
option_3_content_en: Create working agreements
option_4_content_en: Handles uncertainties, risks, and changes

content_en: The project you are leading is supposed to upgrade the application developed by your company on desktop computers and mobile devices. Last week, a major supplier of electronics unexpectedly released a new mobile device. You realize that your application, with a little bit of modification, can run much faster and more securely on the new device. What should you do next in regards to this opportunity?
option_1_content_en: Create a cost forecast and communicate it to stakeholders
option_2_content_en: Submit a change request to modify the application
option_3_content_en: Update project funding requirements in consideration for the unexpected work
option_4_content_en: Conduct variance analysis for an appropriate reserve amount

content_en: You are leading a project that was supposed to be managed using agile methods. Every week, however, the product owner holds a five-hour backlog refinement meeting with the project team where she presents the project scope broken down to the work package level. After three iterations, the project team's velocity is slower than expected. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Ask the product owner to decompose the scope down to the task level and assign the tasks to the team members
option_2_content_en: Advise the product owner to hold two five-hour backlog refinement meetings per week to gain further clarity on the scope
option_3_content_en: Coach the product owner on presenting the overall story concept with one-hour weekly backlog refinement meetings
option_4_content_en: Hold a team-building exercise with the team members and product owner to improve the communication between them

content_en: The project management plan and the performance measurement baseline have been approved. As you monitor the project's progress, you realize the approved budget is limiting the project and will affect the targeted completion date. This constraint could affect the company's success in the new venture. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Use the contingency reserves
option_2_content_en: Use the management reserves
option_3_content_en: Cut costs to stay within the budget
option_4_content_en: Ask for a change in the budget

content_en: You and your project team have just completed the development of the project management plan for your agile project. You have requested one of the team members to schedule a meeting to present the finalized project management plan. The team member has asked who should be invited to the meeting. How should you respond?
option_1_content_en: Invite the customer only because it is an agile project
option_2_content_en: Find the answer in the organization process assets
option_3_content_en: Invite only the project sponsor and the project team
option_4_content_en: Consult the project schedule network diagram

content_en: You are a scrum master leading an agile project team that has been consistently meeting the goals set for each iteration. The product owner is pleased with the team's progress, and the performance measurement baseline shows no deviations. However, you feel that one team member is less productive than the others. What is the most appropriate feedback approach for you to take in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Allow the project team members to address the issue if they deem necessary
option_2_content_en: Direct the underperforming team member to work extra hours to bridge the gap
option_3_content_en: Call out the team member's low productivity at the upcoming iteration retrospective
option_4_content_en: From the next iteration onward, assign the team member the easiest user stories

content_en: As part of the Develop Schedule process, the project manager creates the project schedule using a Gantt chart. Three Scrum teams will develop the project deliverables. Due to dependencies, the teams will be required to coordinate their work twice a week using extended standup meetings. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Submit a change request to switch the Gantt chart to burndown chart
option_2_content_en: Include Scrum of Scrums (SoS) meetings in the project schedule
option_3_content_en: Crash the schedule to eliminate the dependencies between the teams
option_4_content_en: Reflect the actual velocity of the teams in the project schedule

content_en: You are managing a project team that has recently been expanded by new team members working remotely from another country. Their roles have been outlined to form a preliminary team charter. Nevertheless, you have noticed a considerable lack of acceptance of cultural differences in the team, resulting in frequent conflicts. Which of the following techniques could help you in this situation? (Choose three)
option_1_content_en: Focus groups
option_2_content_en: Role definition
option_3_content_en: Ground rules
option_4_content_en: Ability tests

content_en: You are a senior project manager who is mentoring a newly promoted project manager. Your mentee states that she has recurring arguments with her project team and is having difficulty controlling her own temper. This situation has created a toxic environment for the project team and threatens the successful completion of the project. What is the best advice for your mentee?
option_1_content_en: Improve leadership skills
option_2_content_en: Develop emotional intelligence
option_3_content_en: Study conflict management
option_4_content_en: Introduce recognition and rewards

content_en: The project manager is 6 months into a multi-million-dollar project. The latest analysis shows a CPI of 1.5 and an SPI of 0.6. What should she do?
option_1_content_en: Nothing. The analysis shows the project is on budget and on schedule.
option_2_content_en: Consider crashing the project schedule
option_3_content_en: Replace one of the higher paid team members with a lower-salaried employee
option_4_content_en: Inform the customer that you are extending the delivery date for the project

content_en: You are leading a software development project for a client. Due to unstable requirements, you have elected to use a change-driven life cycle. You are currently facilitating an iteration planning meeting with the product owner and the development team. What should you do as part of the meeting?
option_1_content_en: Control the scope to prevent scope creep
option_2_content_en: Review the product increment and get feedback
option_3_content_en: Make sure the scope of the iteration is fixed
option_4_content_en: Recommend improvements for the next iteration

content_en: You have been assigned to lead an initiative for which the business case has not been sufficiently made to get approval to initiate a hybrid project. In some of the past projects, teams realized too late into project execution that no one in the company had the skills needed to build some of the features, so it was developed by a contractor, resulting in cost overruns. What would you do differently in your assignment to avoid cost overruns?
option_1_content_en: Start with a proof of concept
option_2_content_en: Use burndown charts for reporting
option_3_content_en: Develop a project charter
option_4_content_en: Encourage team knowledge sharing

content_en: A project manager is developing a quality management plan for a project to design a medical device. Given the nature of the product, quality will play a vital role. Additionally, the acceptance criteria for the project deliverables will have a direct impact on quality standards. The project manager wants to gain an understanding of the acceptance criteria. What document should the project manager review for this purpose?
option_1_content_en: The project charter
option_2_content_en: The requirements management plan
option_3_content_en: The scope statement
option_4_content_en: The acceptance criteria register

content_en: As project execution begins, the project manager acquires the project team and, based on project needs, decides that the team will use Scrum to develop the product of the project. After conducting an assessment of the project team's Scrum skillset, the project manager realizes that according to the Shu-Ha-Ri model, the team is at the Shu level. What should the project manager recommend to the team?
option_1_content_en: Request project termination
option_2_content_en: Modify Scrum to fit the project needs
option_3_content_en: Develop a new agile method
option_4_content_en: Closely follow Scrum ceremonies

content_en: The project manager and a stakeholder get into a heated debate about the stakeholder's idea requiring a scope change to the project. The project manager says the change will not be implemented and that the stakeholder must drop the idea. The project manager emphasizes that she is the project manager and the decision is final. Should the project manager have responded differently to resolve the conflict?
option_1_content_en: No; The project manager has the formal authority to make the final decision.
option_2_content_en: Yes; The project manager should have discussed the idea with other stakeholders.
option_3_content_en: No; The project manager was demonstrating the culture in which the company works.
option_4_content_en: Yes; The project manager should have compromised with the stakeholder.

content_en: You are leading a hybrid project with an agile team developing the web application and a traditional engineering team to design the servers that will host the application. You want to determine what does your company say about the use of social media tools to communicate and work with the stakeholders to meet their needs and expectations. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Review the stakeholder register
option_2_content_en: Check the organizational process assets
option_3_content_en: Consult with the project sponsor
option_4_content_en: Check the lessons learned repository

content_en: You are attempting to coordinate activities between your project, another related project, and operations, all of which are being managed as a group. A conflict has arisen over control of a key resource that is vital to both projects as well as operations. The conflict has reached an impasse and needs to be resolved by a higher authority. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Discuss the problem with the portfolio manager
option_2_content_en: Escalate the issue to the operations manager
option_3_content_en: Raise the issue with the other project manager
option_4_content_en: Request help from the project management office

content_en: A project manager is determining the budget for a software development project where the product will be built incrementally. Since the project is subject to a strict budget, the project manager has to ensure that scope and schedule baselines stay within cost constraints. The project manager includes budgetary requirements in the release plan. How can the information in the release plan help the project manager with determining the project budget?
option_1_content_en: The release plan can become a part of the cost management plan.
option_2_content_en: The velocity can be increased for the project to stay within budget constraints.
option_3_content_en: Release burndown charts can be updated with cost trend lines.
option_4_content_en: Review meetings with stakeholders can be used to discuss the scope and schedule.

content_en: You are leading a software development project using agile methodologies. If the project is successful, it will open up vast opportunities for future revenue and growth. The project has a high risk of failure, but the potential benefits outweigh the risks. These risks and rewards must be considered when selecting the content of each iteration. Which features should be prioritized and developed first in this scenario?
option_1_content_en: High-value and low-risk features
option_2_content_en: Low-value and low-risk features
option_3_content_en: High-value and high-risk features
option_4_content_en: Low-value and high-risk features

content_en: A project manager is explaining the roles and responsibilities for the quality assurance process with the project team. Who will play a role in this process?
option_1_content_en: The project manager, project team, and management of the performing organization
option_2_content_en: The project sponsor along with the project manager and project team
option_3_content_en: The project manager along with the project team
option_4_content_en: The project manager, project team, project sponsor, management of the performing organization, and the customer

content_en: Two days before the end of the last iteration of the project, an agile coach has noticed that the performance of one of the developers significantly degraded, risking the iteration goal. The coach and the developer have a one-on-one coaching meeting scheduled a day after the iteration's end date. What is the best course of action for the agile coach to take in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Conduct the individual performance appraisal of the developer
option_2_content_en: Ask the team to swarm on the tasks assigned to the developer
option_3_content_en: Employ real-time feedback to address the issue with the developer
option_4_content_en: Wait for the one-on-one meeting scheduled with the developer

content_en: After the project team has completed their first iteration, you are requested to provide the project's status report to the sponsor. You collect the following data: The cost baseline for the entire project is $528,000. The schedule baseline provides for six two-week iterations. The actual costs associated with the first iteration were $80,000. The team completed 45 of 50 story points planned for the first iteration. What should you report to the sponsor?
option_1_content_en: The team's velocity in the first iteration is zero
option_2_content_en: The team's velocity in the first iteration is 50
option_3_content_en: The SPI for the first iteration is 0.9
option_4_content_en: The CPI for the first iteration is 1.1

content_en: An organization is transitioning from predictive project management to agile. As a project manager, your upcoming project will require compliance reporting that will need to be submitted to internal auditors due to regulatory oversight. How might you address the need for compliance reporting in this hybrid environment?
option_1_content_en: Work with the auditors to streamline the process
option_2_content_en: Task one of the team members to complete the compliance reporting
option_3_content_en: Transfer the responsibility of compliance reporting to the legal department
option_4_content_en: Avoid agile as it not suitable for projects that operate in a regulatory environment

content_en: You are leading an agile software development project. During a sprint review, the customer rejects the deliverables stating that the grade is acceptable but not the quality. Of the following, which might be the best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Add another developer to increase velocity
option_2_content_en: Remove some of the features and focus on quality for the next iteration
option_3_content_en: Increase the number of features for the next sprint
option_4_content_en: Introduce more rigorous testing during the next sprint to reduce bugs

content_en: You are managing a project to build 100 site towers, and you have just completed building the 50th tower. To mark the successful completion of this first significant milestone, you hold a celebration where you share the developments, challenges, and lessons learned so far on the project. In what process will you use this information and knowledge gained so far to improve the future performance of the project?
option_1_content_en: Control Quality
option_2_content_en: Perform Continuous Improvement
option_3_content_en: Manage Quality
option_4_content_en: Direct and Manage Project Work

content_en: You are leading a project with a critical time constraint and cannot afford any project delays. An argument between two project team members over a report format to document their testing results turns into a shouting match. The team members draw you into their argument. You realize that resolving the conflict would delay the project timeline. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Tell the team members to figure it out for themselves
option_2_content_en: Look for an approach that would completely satisfy both team members
option_3_content_en: Request the team members to go back to work to avoid any further delays
option_4_content_en: Select the report format that you think is best and make the decision

content_en: The PMBOK® Guide defines project charter as a document that "formally authorizes the existence of a project and provides the project manager with the authority to apply organizational resources to project activities." Developing project charters on agile projects:
option_1_content_en: Must follow the PMBOK® Guide processes
option_2_content_en: Must not follow the PMBOK® Guide processes
option_3_content_en: Is not required because Agile is paperless
option_4_content_en: Does not necessarily require a formal document

content_en: You are managing a project with stakeholders from many different departments including marketing, engineering, and information technology. As you are monitoring stakeholder engagement, it becomes clear to you that stakeholders from the marketing department who used to be supportive appear to be neutral. After researching the reasons for the gap, you discover the marketing department views the project communications to be too technical, leading them to lose interest in the project. What might be your next step?
option_1_content_en: Perform a communication styles assessment
option_2_content_en: Provide technical training for the marketing department
option_3_content_en: Update the communications management plan
option_4_content_en: Review the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix

content_en: To ensure that lessons learned are captured and documented throughout the project life cycle, the project manager creates the lessons learned register. What project management process is being performed?
option_1_content_en: Direct and Manage Project Work
option_2_content_en: Monitor and Control Project Work
option_3_content_en: Manage Project Knowledge
option_4_content_en: Create Lessons Learned

content_en: The project requires ongoing stakeholder engagement and needs to respond to high levels of change. The project manager has chosen an adaptive life cycle for the project. The backlog contains an ordered list of requirements and work. At the beginning of each iteration, the team determines how many of the items on the backlog can be delivered within the next iteration. Which process(es) will the project team need to repeat with each iteration?
option_1_content_en: Define Scope
option_2_content_en: Collect Requirements and Create WBS
option_3_content_en: Collect Requirements and Define Scope
option_4_content_en: Collect Requirements, Define Scope, and Create WBS

content_en: You meet with your team and key stakeholders to decide on what approach, waterfall or agile, should be used for your project. You explain to the meeting participants that continuous improvement is of utmost priority for the project. Someone asks you how waterfall methodologies compare with agile as it relates to continuous improvement. How should you respond to this question?
option_1_content_en: Waterfall takes a more proactive approach to continuous improvement, comparing to agile which is more reactive.
option_2_content_en: Agile projects conduct retrospectives during project execution but not at the end of the project as in waterfall.
option_3_content_en: Agile teams tend to be more focused on continuous improvement and will review performance more regularly.
option_4_content_en: Continuous improvement is handled essentially the same in agile and waterfall project management frameworks.

content_en: A project manager is implementing the quality management plan for a project to construct a natural gas pipeline. During this process, an internal audit discovers that while the project meets all applicable government regulations, there is a discrepancy with ISO 9000 criteria. Which tailoring consideration did the project manager most likely neglect earlier in the project?
option_1_content_en: Continuous improvement
option_2_content_en: Standards and regulatory compliance
option_3_content_en: Project life cycle
option_4_content_en: Since the project meets all applicable government regulations, nothing was missed earlier in the project

content_en: As a project manager, you recently completed a project team performance appraisal, and a previously unknown competency gap in technical skills was uncovered, which needs to be addressed. What should you do next?
option_1_content_en: Implement the response planned for this risk
option_2_content_en: Conduct unplanned training to address the competency gap
option_3_content_en: Consult the training management plan
option_4_content_en: Let go of the staff who have technical skill gaps

content_en: You are leading two independent teams working on the same project. The nature of the deliverables requires that one team takes a predictive approach, while the other uses Scrum. Due to dependencies between the teams and the variable nature of the outputs from the Scrum team, the predictive team needs to confirm their understanding of the Scrum team's activities with the shortest feedback loop possible. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Include a project retrospective into the project schedule
option_2_content_en: Request that the Scrum team use information radiators
option_3_content_en: Incorporate the use of periodic customer feedback loops
option_4_content_en: Have the predictive team attend the daily scrum meetings

content_en: A project manager and team are in the process of finalizing all project activities. They have obtained final acceptance and transferred ownership of deliverables, obtained administrative closure, collated lessons learned, archived all project documents, and obtained feedback from relevant stakeholders. Finally, the project manager and team have been released and reassigned to other assignments. Based on the information provided, what might have been forgotten?
option_1_content_en: Reviewing project requirements
option_2_content_en: Verifying project deliverables
option_3_content_en: Sharing the final project report
option_4_content_en: Conducting benefit analysis

content_en: A new developer joins the project. However, her productivity is limited since she lacks the competency in one of the programming languages. This language is not only used on this project but will also be required on future projects. Training costs were not included in the project budget, and the project CPI is 0.75. What is the best course of action for the project manager?
option_1_content_en: Submit a change request to update the development approach
option_2_content_en: Seek approval for the performing organization to absorb the training costs
option_3_content_en: Stop using this programming language on this project
option_4_content_en: Terminate the employment of the new developer and find a replacement

content_en: In their first iteration, an agile team completed only half of the planned work. It turns out that before the current project began, the team members were requested to provide ongoing support for the prior release. Angry project stakeholders meet with the scrum master and complain that supporting prior releases should have never been included in the project plans. How should the scrum master respond?
option_1_content_en: Agree with the stakeholders and remove all further support work from the next iterations
option_2_content_en: Ignore the stakeholders' complain and instruct the team to continue supporting the prior releases
option_3_content_en: Explain that routine work of supporting prior releases may be included in project plans
option_4_content_en: Request that from now on the team work overtime to complete both the planned work and support

content_en: The deliverables of a two-year-long project have just been accepted. It is four months late, but the customer is pleased to have it. The project manager is glad to be done with the deliverables but is concerned about the cost and schedule overruns. He decides to re-run the initial cost-benefit analysis using the actual project costs. Where should the project manager obtain the initial cost-benefit analysis?
option_1_content_en: From the customer
option_2_content_en: The project charter
option_3_content_en: The business case
option_4_content_en: The benefits management plan

content_en: A project manager creates a procurement statement of work (SOW) from the project scope baseline. The scope of the SOW, however, is not yet well defined, therefore the project manager decides to contract with a vendor to provide an agile team of programmers. The contract is structured with fixed-price increments based on user stories. How might the project manager verify that the vendor has met the contractual obligations?
option_1_content_en: Wait until the team completes the development of all user stories specified in the SOW
option_2_content_en: Request the product owner to approve or reject user stories during a sprint review
option_3_content_en: Validate the user stories as soon as they are completed at any point during a sprint
option_4_content_en: Conduct a procurement audit with the vendor each time a sprint retrospective is held

content_en: As a scrum master, you are facilitating a retrospective for a sprint that failed to meet all of its objectives. Members of the development team and the product owner are arguing over who is responsible for the failure. After performing a root cause analysis, you uncover the source of the conflict. Of the following, what did you most likely discover?
option_1_content_en: The product owner determined how many user stories were to be completed during the sprint
option_2_content_en: The development team decided how many user stories were to be completed during the sprint
option_3_content_en: You, as the scrum master, failed to assign user stories to the development team
option_4_content_en: The Gantt chart did not include enough story points

content_en: The quality management has been perfect for the project up to this point. Suddenly, the quality assurance (QA) lead who developed and performed most of the quality activities for the project has been temporarily reassigned to help another project. What should the project manager do?
option_1_content_en: Submit a change request to adjust the cost baseline and the schedule baseline
option_2_content_en: Request the team to develop replacement quality activities
option_3_content_en: Assign another team member to carry out the originally planned quality activities
option_4_content_en: Pause quality activities until the QA lead returns to the project

content_en:
A project manager is reviewing a document where information about problems impacting project performance is recorded and monitored. According to the document, a new problem that was logged yesterday by a project team member indicates that delays have just exceeded the established schedule variance threshold and corrective action is required. No additional details about the new problem are provided in the document. 

What should the project manager do immediately?
option_1_content_en: Assign a responsible party to follow up on the problem
option_2_content_en: Record the disposition of the change request
option_3_content_en: Send the project progress report to the stakeholders
option_4_content_en: Update the lessons learned register

content_en: Midway into project execution, a key stakeholder leaves the company. A new stakeholder fills in the vacant role. The project manager understands that the stakeholder engagement plan should be updated to reflect the strategies and actions required to involve the new stakeholder in the project. The project manager meets with the new stakeholder for an interview. Which of the following questions would be the most helpful for the project manager in updating the plan? (Choose four)
option_1_content_en: Have you ever managed a project before?
option_2_content_en: How much risk are you willing to take for an anticipated benefit?
option_3_content_en: What position did you hold in your previous company?
option_4_content_en: What are your communication preferences?
option_5_content_en: Which information serves as input or is a tool and technique in the plan stakeholder engagement process?
option_6_content_en: Which information is likely to be found elsewhere?

content_en: You have been assigned to lead an agile project. You want to ensure that project information is shared within and across the organization, so that any misalignments, dependencies, or other issues related to the frequently changing requirements are surfaced as quickly as possible. How could this goal be best achieved?
option_1_content_en: By distributing the project report weekly
option_2_content_en: By inviting stakeholders to daily standups
option_3_content_en: By promoting aggressive transparency
option_4_content_en: By sharing comprehensive documentation

content_en: You are planning a kick-off meeting for your new project. The meeting will communicate the start of the project, key milestones, and other relevant information. Which of the following best describes the objective of this meeting?
option_1_content_en: Inform and engage stakeholders and gain commitment
option_2_content_en: Manage threats and opportunities throughout the project
option_3_content_en: Ensure that the project is completed on schedule and budget
option_4_content_en: Secure resources required to complete project deliverables

content_en: You are leading a project to develop a product that will be sold through an existing nationwide dealer network. The product will be built incrementally by a virtual team, while the dealer training and product rollout processes will be well-defined upfront. You want the dealers to provide the team with regular feedback throughout product development? What is the best strategy to achieve your goal?
option_1_content_en: Suggest that the dealers attend the biweekly iteration retrospective meetings
option_2_content_en: Collect requirements upfront and develop a detailed WBS for product development
option_3_content_en: Invite the dealers to attend product demonstrations via video conference
option_4_content_en: Colocate the dealers with some of the developers for the duration of the project

content_en: A project manager is leading an agile research and development project. The project team is using a diagram, which breaks down the causes of an identified problem into discrete branches to determine the main cause of the problem. Which diagram might the project team be using in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Pareto diagram
option_2_content_en: Matrix diagram
option_3_content_en: Tornado diagram
option_4_content_en: Ishikawa diagram

content_en: You have been assigned to lead an agile project. The project team is comprised of experienced agile practitioners who have been working together for a long time. In this agile environment, what is the best approach for you to take to manage project integration?
option_1_content_en: Develop the project management plan that integrates all project activities
option_2_content_en: Let the team determine how plans and components should be integrated
option_3_content_en: Seek approval to hire an external project integration management expert
option_4_content_en: In agile environments, project integration management is not applicable

content_en: You are leading a construction project that involves a vendor. A team member tells you that based on the rough assessment of the vendor's current work in progress, she suspects that the vendor will be unable to complete their work on time. You share your concerns with the vendor, but they claim that they are progressing as planned. What is your best course of action to ensure a mutual understanding of the work in progress?
option_1_content_en: Conduct a walkthrough
option_2_content_en: Perform an earned value analysis (EVA)
option_3_content_en: Conduct an audit
option_4_content_en: Resort to alternative dispute resolution (ADR)

content_en: An organization has established a controlling project management office (PMO). The first task of the PMO is to update the guidelines for project compliance in the organization. Which of the following could the PMO enforce? (Choose three)
option_1_content_en: Use of particular project management methodologies
option_2_content_en: Adoption of specific templates, forms, and tools
option_3_content_en: Adherence to local health regulations
option_4_content_en: Conformance to governance frameworks

content_en: You have just been assigned to an upcoming agile project. As part of pre-project work, you review all of the organization's policies and procedures regarding compliance. You realize that only some of them may be applicable to your project. What should you do first?
option_1_content_en: Switch the project management approach from agile to traditional
option_2_content_en: Incorporate all compliance policies and procedures in the implementation strategy
option_3_content_en: Ensure compliance activities are included in the project schedule baseline
option_4_content_en: Classify the compliance categories to determine the expenditure of project resources

content_en: A scrum master is leading an agile project in which the development team has failed to achieve the sprint goal for the past three iterations. During the sprint retrospective, the team decides to implement several changes to improve velocity. How might the scrum master verify any performance improvement?
option_1_content_en: Calculate the project's CPI
option_2_content_en: Create a burndown chart
option_3_content_en: Review the burnup chart
option_4_content_en: Study the Gantt chart

content_en: A new smartphone will be developed by two teams: a hardware team that will use a predictive project management approach and a software team that will use an agile framework. Each team is colocated but resides in two different parts of the country. The teams will need to coordinate their activities very closely, but bringing them together in one location is not an option. What should the project manager do to create the most collaborative environment?
option_1_content_en: Use a blended agile approach
option_2_content_en: Create a fishbowl window
option_3_content_en: Transition the hardware team to agile
option_4_content_en: Implement caves and common

content_en: Due to an uncertain market environment and complexity of upcoming projects, your company is considering a transition from a traditional to hybrid project management approach. The company tasks you with researching various options for incorporating new project management practices that would help the company move closer to its goal. Which of the following would you least likely recommend?
option_1_content_en: Involving business analysts in requirements management
option_2_content_en: Increasing the level of detail during initial project planning
option_3_content_en: Implementing tools to identify complex project elements
option_4_content_en: Incorporating agile, incremental, and iterative practices

content_en: You are the project manager for the initial design phase of a new ergonomic pen. You have conducted multiple interviews with pen users and have tested various design concepts. Your most recent design has been verified and accepted by key stakeholders. The pen design is ready to transition to the team managing the next phase. Which of the following should you consult to find out who will take ownership of the pen design?
option_1_content_en: The project management plan
option_2_content_en: The final report
option_3_content_en: The scope statement
option_4_content_en: The communications management plan

content_en: You review the WBS of your project and realize that due to the lack of in-house expertise, some of the deliverables will need to be outsourced to a vendor. However, the requirements for these deliverables are not well-understood at the moment. Therefore, you decide that the outsourced portion of work will need to be managed using an agile framework. What is your best approach in negotiating an agreement with the vendor?
option_1_content_en: Seek an informal agreement rather than a formal contract
option_2_content_en: Secure a fixed-price contract for the outsourced scope
option_3_content_en: Negotiate aggressively for the most advantageous terms
option_4_content_en: Pursue a shared-risk-reward contract relationships

content_en: A project manager is considering to change the Control Costs process currently used on her project. Instead of submitting budget change requests to the CCB, she wants to invite stakeholders to the parking lot portion of the daily standups and discuss requested changes there. The project manager meets with the stakeholders to propose the process change. Which of the following arguments would least likely to convince the stakeholders of the benefits of the new process?
option_1_content_en: The cost management and change management plans will be updated to reflect the new process.
option_2_content_en: Earned value analysis data from a previous project will be compared to iterative data accumulation.
option_3_content_en: Only those budget change requests that do not affect the project cost baseline will be discussed.
option_4_content_en: Other project managers in the organization going through similar process changes will be consulted.

content_en: A project manager has just calculated the project performance measurements, and the project's current cost performance index (CPI) is 0.9 while the schedule performance index (SPI) is 1.1. Which of the following is correct regarding the project's performance status?
option_1_content_en: Over budget and ahead of schedule
option_2_content_en: Under budget and behind schedule
option_3_content_en: Over budget and behind schedule
option_4_content_en: Under budget and ahead of schedule

content_en: A vendor has been contracted by a buyer to develop a new device. The vendor insisted that the contract thoroughly capture the device specifications. The buyer does not have clear requirements upfront and, therefore, requested that the vendor develop the device using agile. The vendor delivers as per the contract, but the buyer is not satisfied with the outcome. Which Agile Manifesto's value was most likely not appropriately applied?
option_1_content_en: Business people and developers must work together
option_2_content_en: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
option_3_content_en: Pair programming over continuous integration
option_4_content_en: Customer collaboration over contract negotiations

content_en: During a meeting, the product owner restated the product vision, described the target user groups, the business goals, and main features to be delivered by the agile project in its upcoming releases. Then, to visually depict these features, the product owner created the product roadmap. Which of the following best describes the purpose of the meeting?
option_1_content_en: Establish a shared project vision among the project stakeholders
option_2_content_en: Create the product backlog for each one of the upcoming releases
option_3_content_en: Establish a shared release vision among the project stakeholders
option_4_content_en: Determine the project scope, schedule, cost, quality, and resources

content_en: You meet with your team to determine the life cycle for your project. After analyzing the best way to define and manage requirements, develop deliverables, handle changes, control risk and cost, and engage key stakeholders, the decision is made to select a hybrid life cycle. With the project life cycle selected, how will the requirements be managed on your project?
option_1_content_en: Defined during the transition to the customer
option_2_content_en: Elaborated at periodic intervals during delivery
option_3_content_en: Defined up-front before development begins
option_4_content_en: Elaborated as often as needed during delivery

content_en: An agile coach joined a team that has been working on a project for the last few months. The coach noticed that the team members were struggling to remove impediments, did not have a discipline around time-boxed events, and were not using information radiators to display the project status. What is the best course of action for the agile coach to take?
option_1_content_en: Help the team deal with impediments, remind of the importance of time-boxing, and force the team to use information radiators
option_2_content_en: Tell the team to deal with impediments, remind of the importance of time-boxing, and suggest the team to use information radiators
option_3_content_en: Help the team to deal with impediments, remind of the importance of time-boxing, and suggest the team to use information radiators
option_4_content_en: Do nothing, since the issues are minor and can be handled by the team because agile teams are self-managing and self-organizing

content_en: A PMO steeped in traditional waterfall project management has hired you, as an agile practitioner, to guide the organization's transformation to agile. After completing an initial assessment of the organizational culture, you have realized that many of the stakeholders are resistant to the change.What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Provide training to ensure the employees are more highly specialized
option_2_content_en: Transition all projects to agile at the same time
option_3_content_en: Seek a high-level executive willing to champion the cause
option_4_content_en: Ensure the work is decomposed into silos

content_en: Monthly audits were performed to determine if project activities comply with corporate policies, procedures, and best practices. Throughout the project, the results of the monthly audits indicated that the team was in compliance. However, at the end of the project, it was determined that some of the project activities did not comply with organizational policies. What most likely caused these compliance gaps to be missed during the audits?
option_1_content_en: The audits were conducted by the company's internal audit department
option_2_content_en: The audits were conducted by one of the project team members
option_3_content_en: The audits were conducted by the project management office (PMO)
option_4_content_en: The audits were conducted by an auditor external to the organization

content_en: During the development of the stakeholder engagement plan, the project manager realizes that a key stakeholder is resistant to the project. Without the support of this stakeholder, the project may fail. What is the best course of action for the project manager to identify the reason for the stakeholder being resistant?
option_1_content_en: Escalate to the project sponsor
option_2_content_en: Update the stakeholder register
option_3_content_en: Use the mind mapping technique
option_4_content_en: Utilize an Ishikawa diagram

content_en: In order to take advantage of the best talent available, a project manager recruits developers internationally rather than just locally. She is delighted to have acquired such highly skilled individuals but now needs to develop them into a cohesive team. Ideally, the project manager would like to bring everyone together at the home office, but the project budget does not allow for travel expenses. What is the best tool or technique for the project manager to use in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Sensitivity analysis
option_2_content_en: Recognition and rewards
option_3_content_en: Virtual teams
option_4_content_en: Colocation

content_en: A project manager invited several vendors to a pre-bid conference. After a private conversation with one of the vendors who had an inquiry about a new mandatory government requirement, the project manager sent an email to the vendor to address the question. The project manager realizes that the requirement should have been included in the project scope baseline and the statement of work (SOW). What should the project manager do in this situation?
option_1_content_en: No further action is needed as the vendor's question have been addressed
option_2_content_en: Update the statement of work and the scope baseline, and communicate the changes to all vendors
option_3_content_en: Update the statement of work and the scope baseline, and hold another pre-bid conference
option_4_content_en: Update the SOW, submit a change request to update the scope baseline, and communicate the changes to all vendors

content_en: While the first phase of a construction project was a success, one of the two lead architects suddenly had to resign from her position due to a conflict of interest within the company. What should the project manager do immediately to manage the team composition?
option_1_content_en: Write a work performance report to generate awareness of the lead architect's departure
option_2_content_en: Update the project organizational chart to reflect the team change
option_3_content_en: Review the change management plan and submit a change request
option_4_content_en: Use float on the critical path to prevent schedule slippage due to this new risk

content_en: A client completed a walkthrough of the deliverables and formally accepted the work. The next day, the project manager returns to the project site to pick up company equipment and make arrangements for final payment. What should the project manager do when meeting the client as part of project closure?
option_1_content_en: Confirm the final acceptance of the deliverable
option_2_content_en: Settle procurement claims
option_3_content_en: Validate the scope objectives have been met
option_4_content_en: Ensure quality assurance was performed

content_en: You are leading an agile project to develop a computer game, which will be broken down into four releases. After the first release, the initial online reviews are poor, and the early adopters have provided detailed feedback about what they don't like about the game. You are concerned about the impact of the poor reviews on future releases. What is the best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Hold a release retrospective
option_2_content_en: Terminate the project
option_3_content_en: Discuss the issue with the project sponsor
option_4_content_en: Expedite the delivery of the second release

content_en: As a project manager, you are leading a colocated project team that will create deliverables in an agile fashion, followed by a rollout phase that will use a predictive approach. You are concerned that the transition from agile to waterfall may cause friction within the project team. With the development phase complete, how might the team's working agreements need to change in this situation?
option_1_content_en: The team charter will need to be updated to reflect collective responsibility for the completion of project tasks.
option_2_content_en: The project manager should institute a set of working agreements that worked well on previous waterfall projects.
option_3_content_en: Each project team member will need to develop their own social contract to support the new framework.
option_4_content_en: The social contract should reflect a transition from collective to individual responsibility for the project tasks.

content_en: You are managing a virtual project team across multiple time zones. As the project progresses, the team members learn to trust one another and adjust their work routines to accommodate the different time zones, work habits, and culture. What stage of team development is being demonstrated in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Forming
option_2_content_en: Storming
option_3_content_en: Performing
option_4_content_en: Norming

content_en: A project manager has been asked to create a document that formally authorizes a project to use ground-penetrating radar to map geological conditions along a proposed crude oil pipeline route. The performing organization has a written formal agreement in place to share the data with a local university. The project manager has reviewed the business documents and considered any relevant external environmental factors to create the requested document. What might the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Research the stakeholder engagement plan for any information to be included in the document
option_2_content_en: Ensure any relevant information from the memorandum of understanding (MOU) is included in the document
option_3_content_en: Review the business case for any pertinent information
option_4_content_en: Look to see if a benefits management plan was previously created

content_en: You are leading a software development project for a client. The change control board (CCB) has been inundated with change requests from the client throughout the project as the product has evolved. This situation drives the team crazy and makes controlling the project scope extremely challenging and time-consuming. Which of the following tailoring considerations might you have missed earlier in the project?
option_1_content_en: Diversity
option_2_content_en: Stability of requirements
option_3_content_en: Physical location
option_4_content_en: Validation and control

content_en: During project execution, the new state-of-the-art technology that is used on the project to produce the deliverables is unstable, which puts the whole project at risk of failure. Your sponsor is on vacation and cannot be reached. To get immediate attention to the issue, you want to know what is the escalation procedure. What should you do next?
option_1_content_en: Consult the communications management plan
option_2_content_en: Consult the risk register
option_3_content_en: Consult the stakeholder engagement plan
option_4_content_en: Submit a change request to replace the technology

content_en: You are in the initiation stage of a project that aims to deploy and then maintain the robotics for an automated production line for an important client. In the project charter, you need to include the agreed mean time to recover (MTTR) in the event of a breakdown. What should you do to find this information?
option_1_content_en: Do nothing since agreements are not yet available during project initiation
option_2_content_en: Refer to the procurement management plan
option_3_content_en: Review any emails or other correspondence with the client
option_4_content_en: Check the service level agreement with the client

content_en: Near the end of an iteration, the project team is ready to lead a product review with the product manager. What is the objective of the review?
option_1_content_en: Validate the product scope
option_2_content_en: Manage product quality
option_3_content_en: Control the product scope
option_4_content_en: Close the project or phase

content_en: While performing monitoring and controlling activities, the project manager discovers inconsistencies between the project management plan and the project's actual performance. She now needs to determine corrective actions to minimize the impact of the inconsistencies on the project. In what project document would she have documented the inconsistencies and would look at to review them?
option_1_content_en: Quality report
option_2_content_en: Change log
option_3_content_en: Assumption log
option_4_content_en: Issue log

content_en: A project manager has just received a signed formalized document as an output from one of the initiation processes in her project. This document was prepared by someone external to the project and will be utilized as a catalyst for the project to move forward. Which of the following describes this document?
option_1_content_en: The business case
option_2_content_en: The scope statement
option_3_content_en: The project charter
option_4_content_en: The approved project plan

content_en: You are managing a project, and members of your project team are at odds about the tasks they are assigned. Disagreements between the team members have escalated and have created a reduction in performance across the project. What tool or technique will you use to address the team's issues and get the project back on track?
option_1_content_en: Networking
option_2_content_en: Recognition and rewards
option_3_content_en: Training
option_4_content_en: Conflict management

content_en: Your project is running behind schedule. To bring the timeline back into alignment with the project management plan, you need some of your project team members to work extra hours. In order to motivate your team, you offer each team member two tickets to a popular sporting event if they work a weekend shift. What type of power are you using in this situation?
option_1_content_en: Managerial
option_2_content_en: Charismatic
option_3_content_en: Persuasive
option_4_content_en: Reward-oriented

content_en: You are creating the schedule to deploy a new ERP software in your company. The company is currently undergoing an agile transformation, so it was decided to develop the new ERP iteratively. The first release of the ERP should be rolled out in four months, and you know that another project, a company-wide operating system upgrade, is scheduled in three months. With the upgrade project affecting your schedule, an impact on which of the following should you assess to determine the number of iterations until rollout?
option_1_content_en: Release planning
option_2_content_en: Product roadmap
option_3_content_en: Iteration backlogs
option_4_content_en: Project charter

content_en: You are leading a project with two dispersed development teams. One team is using traditional waterfall methods, and the other is using XP for product development. Budgetary constraints prevent any of the team members from being colocated. What should you prioritize for team collaboration?
option_1_content_en: Documenting collaboration requirements of the XP team in the communications management plan
option_2_content_en: Setting up remote pairing for the XP team and providing video conferencing capabilities for both teams
option_3_content_en: Allocating dedicated portions of the offices to support the caves and common practice for both teams
option_4_content_en: No specific considerations are required as both teams can learn to collaborate as they do their job

content_en: Development team members argue with the product owner who rejected a deliverable the team developed during the recent iteration. The project manager schedules a meeting with the team, product owner, and other relevant stakeholders to break down the situation and identify the root cause of a misunderstanding. Which of the following will be considered an antipattern if used during the meeting?
option_1_content_en: Drawing a fishbone diagram
option_2_content_en: Using the five whys method
option_3_content_en: Maximizing the number of action items
option_4_content_en: Defining the problem statement

content_en: After an agile team completes three iterations, the project manager determines that the average velocity of the team for these three iterations was 30 story points. There are 292 more story points to complete the remaining portion of the project. How many additional iterations will it take for the team to complete the project?
option_1_content_en: 7 iterations
option_2_content_en: 8 iterations
option_3_content_en: 9 iterations
option_4_content_en: 10 iterations

content_en: You are leading a project to be developed incrementally in small releases. Requirements have been established for the initial release. Feedback from a focus group will determine the scope of each subsequent release. The client has established a strict budget for the entire project. In this adaptive environment, which is the best way to proceed?
option_1_content_en: Use a traditional waterfall approach for the project
option_2_content_en: Add prioritized features to the project scope with each release until the budget is exhausted
option_3_content_en: During initial project planning, develop a detailed budget for each release
option_4_content_en: Use a change control board (CCB) to prevent scope creep

content_en: As the project manager, you are in the process of developing a draft of a document that authorizes a new software development project. You have reviewed the agreements and both business documents. What else should be done as part of this process?
option_1_content_en: Identify stakeholders and prepare the stakeholder register
option_2_content_en: Study the governance functions and processes to provide guidance and decision making
option_3_content_en: Update the business documents to correct any errors
option_4_content_en: Review the benefits management plan

content_en: Late in a project, a key team member leaves the company. The project manager realizes that he does not have enough team members to meet the hard deadline. At a weekly status meeting, the project manager discusses several options with his project team, including authorizing additional overtime, hiring subcontractors, or bringing in additional resources from another project team within the company. Which resource management technique does the project manager use?
option_1_content_en: Cost-benefit analysis
option_2_content_en: Alternatives analysis
option_3_content_en: Problem solving
option_4_content_en: Interpersonal skills

content_en: You are the project manager for a project that is in its early stages. During a meeting, your boss informs you that senior management would like you to include a particular staff member on your project team because of their necessary expertise. You have not recruited any other team members, and the project has not even been formally authorized yet. How should you handle senior management's request?
option_1_content_en: Deny the request because the project manager should be the one to acquire project resources.
option_2_content_en: Accept the request, since identifying specific resources for the project can occur as part of the early planning process.
option_3_content_en: Accept the request only after you have finished creating the project management plan.
option_4_content_en: Deny the request since you have not had an opportunity to verify that the individual has the proper skills.

content_en: The first phase of a software development project that was conducted using a predictive project management approach is over. The project enters its second phase which will require the project team to utilize an eXtreme Programming (XP) method to develop the rest of the product. How might the team ground rules need to be updated?
option_1_content_en: Acceptance of collective responsibility for the project's deliverables
option_2_content_en: Addition of agreements for working in a virtual environment
option_3_content_en: The ground rules will no longer be needed as the team will use XP
option_4_content_en: Accountability for the creation of highly detailed documentation

content_en: Two project team members have had frequent clashes, which have at times resulted in shouting matches during team meetings. The project manager has intervened, asked them to resolve their differences, and even facilitated a meeting between them, but things have gotten worse. The project manager is concerned that the situation is negatively affecting team cohesion and is placing the successful completion of the project at risk. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Use formal procedures including disciplinary actions
option_2_content_en: Allow the team members to resolve their differences on their own
option_3_content_en: Facilitate another meeting between the two team members
option_4_content_en: Request that the other project team members intercede as a form of peer pressure

content_en: The agile project team members are all working in an open office space arrangement. There are many conversations happening concurrently throughout the day. Which of the following is the best option for the project manager?
option_1_content_en: Schedule frequent team checkpoints and post project artifacts in a transparent fashion
option_2_content_en: Request team members to hold off their conversations until formal meeting times
option_3_content_en: Record the conversations and post them in a shared repository
option_4_content_en: Designate afternoons as quiet work times

content_en: A project manager is estimating the length of time the project will take. The project manager worked on a comparable project two years ago that installed 10 miles of guardrails at a rate of one mile a day in similar weather conditions, using the same size crew on the same type of highway. What estimating technique would be the appropriate option for the project manager to use for his duration estimate?
option_1_content_en: Parametric estimating
option_2_content_en: Analogous estimating
option_3_content_en: Bottom-up estimating
option_4_content_en: Three-point estimating

content_en: During a sprint retrospective, the team members complain that the business analyst has been unresponsive to clarify the work package to be developed in the sprint. As a result, the work package has not been accepted by the customer. The scrum master reaches out to the business analyst and requests them to collaborate with the team during the upcoming sprints. What else should the scrum master do?
option_1_content_en: No further action needed as the problem is resolved
option_2_content_en: Report a work ethics violation to the human resources department
option_3_content_en: Continue monitoring the business analyst's involvement
option_4_content_en: Instruct the team to fix the work package to meet customer needs

content_en: A project team that is experienced in the waterfall project management approach has been assigned to their first agile project. To make the transition easier, it has been decided to keep some elements of the waterfall approach in place. During the iteration review, it was realized that a misunderstanding among the development team has led to a duplication of efforts. How might the project manager address this issue?
option_1_content_en: Bring up the topic during the upcoming iteration retrospective
option_2_content_en: Do nothing since the team members are transitioning from waterfall to agile
option_3_content_en: Fallback to a waterfall project management framework going forward
option_4_content_en: Submit a change request to update the communications management plan

content_en: Your company has been contracted by a client for a software development project. The project will use agile methods to deliver product increments. For the client, however, this project will be their first experience with agile. You want to make sure that the client gains the full benefit of early and continuous delivery of software. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Develop a change management plan to address the inevitable changes
option_2_content_en: Request the client to take part in product testing to speed up delivery
option_3_content_en: Gain alignment with the client on the timing of project deliverables
option_4_content_en: Instruct the project team to develop all features in a single release

content_en: It has been decided that the project will be managed using waterfall. However, due to ambiguous requirements, the software will be developed in short iterations using Scrum. After acquiring a team from within the organization, the project manager realizes that the organization lacks technical expertise in several key areas and will require external resources from a vendor. The organization, however, wants to preserve its strategic discretion on the work performed. What is the best contracting technique for the project manager to use to maximize collaboration with the vendor?
option_1_content_en: Team augmentation
option_2_content_en: Early cancellation option
option_3_content_en: Fixed-price increments
option_4_content_en: Not-to-exceed time and materials

content_en: As your project progresses, a team member suggests a minor modification to one of the project deliverables, saying that the modification will improve the overall performance of the final product. You believe that the modification constitutes a minor change to the project scope, schedule, and budget, and should be approved without going to the change control board. What should you do next?
option_1_content_en: Approve the change request. As the project manager, you should use expert judgment to decide what is best for the project.
option_2_content_en: Meet with the change control board members individually and try to persuade them to approve the change request.
option_3_content_en: Submit the change request to the change control board and abide by their decision.
option_4_content_en: Review the change management plan and follow the established process for processing change requests.

content_en: For the third consecutive time, at the end of each iteration, a software application developed by the team fails during the Control Quality process conducted by the quality assurance (QA) department. This situation causes rework for the product and a delay in the project schedule. The project manager wants to reduce the feedback loop to the shortest possible interval. What is the best course of action for the project manager?
option_1_content_en: Shorten the iteration length
option_2_content_en: Reduce the size of the user stories
option_3_content_en: Revise the schedule baseline
option_4_content_en: Suggest pair programming to the team

content_en: An agile team member encounters a technical issue while developing one of the user stories she selected for the current sprint. After multiple unsuccessful attempts to resolve the issue, the team member approaches the scrum master for advice. What is the best course of action for the scrum master?
option_1_content_en: Request that the rest of the team members swarm on the user story
option_2_content_en: Replace the team member with another more experienced one
option_3_content_en: Ask the product owner who wrote the user story to resolve the issue
option_4_content_en: Recommend that the team member try other alternative solutions

content_en: A company is experiencing exponential growth and will soon run out of space in their current production facility. A needs assessment has been completed to evaluate alternatives. One of the options to support future growth is to build an expansion on to their existing production facility. What should the company do next?
option_1_content_en: Collect requirements and develop the project management plan
option_2_content_en: Understand the business goals and objectives to recommend proposals
option_3_content_en: Prepare the business case and benefits management plan
option_4_content_en: Perform the processes within the Initiating Process Group

content_en: You are halfway through a project, which has experienced several setbacks due to unanticipated problems. Based on recent feedback, you are concerned that critical support for the project among key stakeholders is eroding. You want to bring the stakeholders together for a meeting to address any concerns and rebuild support for the project. Which of the following meetings would be the most beneficial for the key stakeholders to attend?
option_1_content_en: Customer wrap-up meeting
option_2_content_en: Change control meeting
option_3_content_en: Celebration meeting
option_4_content_en: Iteration retrospective

content_en: You are leading an off-grid housing construction project. Each of the ten homes in the development will have solar shingles to generate energy and a novel energy storage system. The performing organization is highly experienced with traditional construction methods, but this is their first project to incorporate energy generation and storage. How might you best support continuous improvement efforts throughout the project?
option_1_content_en: Construct the homes sequentially using a predictive model and hold a retrospective after the completion of each home
option_2_content_en: Review the lessons learned repository during project planning and apply the knowledge gained during project execution
option_3_content_en: Build all of the homes concurrently using a predictive approach and update the lessons learned register continuously
option_4_content_en: Utilize an incremental project management approach for the development of the homes and hold a project retrospective

content_en: An agile coach has been nurturing and growing team members through and beyond their current roles. This helped several team members to develop their personal and professional skills to the level where they felt that they outgrew their roles. Eventually, some of them left the team to pursue new opportunities within the organization and outside of it. Was the agile coach right in her approach?
option_1_content_en: No, agile leaders must ensure the team members never leave their teams
option_2_content_en: Yes, agile leaders should develop team members even if that means losing them
option_3_content_en: No, agile leaders may develop team members but not beyond their current roles
option_4_content_en: Yes, agile leaders have to make sure team members eventually leave the team

content_en: To engage the newly identified stakeholders in the project at the earliest opportunity, the scrum master suggests inviting them to the upcoming sprint review meeting to demonstrate to the stakeholders that the team is moving in the right direction and get feedback from the stakeholders about what the team has accomplished. Which of the following is another reason for inviting the stakeholders to this meeting?
option_1_content_en: To reflect on the team performance
option_2_content_en: To prioritize high-risk user stories for the next sprint
option_3_content_en: To reprioritize the release backlog
option_4_content_en: To discuss the high-level plans for the next sprint

content_en: During an initial project planning meeting, the project team decides to save a portion of cost estimates in the work package to offset the potential risk of advances in technology, which would make their current equipment obsolete. What is the best course of action for the project manager?
option_1_content_en: Create a management reserve
option_2_content_en: Submit a change request
option_3_content_en: Create a contingency reserve
option_4_content_en: Do nothing as the risk has not yet realized

content_en: At the daily scrum meeting, a team member brings up a problem accessing a database that impedes his progress. Another team member offers a possible solution, which triggers a conversation between the two. After a few minutes, the scrum master cuts off their conversation, reminding them that the daily scrum is not the appropriate venue for their discussion. What should the scrum master do next?
option_1_content_en: Submit a change request to the database team so that the problem gets resolved and impediment removed
option_2_content_en: Request that the team members swarm on the database problem and resolve it as soon as possible
option_3_content_en: Suggest the two team members place the issue in the parking lot and discuss it once the meeting is over
option_4_content_en: Allow the conversation between the two team members to continue until the issue is resolved

content_en: Four vendors have responded to a bid request on your project. Which of the following vendors should you select based on the expected monetary value (EMV)?
option_1_content_en: Vendor 1 with an 80% probability of success and profit of $20,000
option_2_content_en: Vendor 2 with a 90% probability of success and profit of $19,000
option_3_content_en: Vendor 3 with a 75% probability of success and profit of $18,000
option_4_content_en: Vendor 4 with an 85% probability of success and profit of $20,000

content_en: You have been assigned to lead a drug development project for a small pharmaceutical company. The drug development aspect of the project is characterized by a high degree of uncertainty, complexity, and risk. The governmental approval process, on the other hand, is highly structured and well defined. What project management approach would you recommend for this project?
option_1_content_en: Agile for the drug development phase, and predictive for the governmental approval process
option_2_content_en: Predictive for the drug development phase, and agile for the governmental approval process
option_3_content_en: Kanban to maximize WIP for compliance activities related to the governmental approval process
option_4_content_en: Crystal clear for both the drug development phase and the governmental approval process

content_en: A project manager has been communicating with 10 stakeholders regularly. Last week 2 more stakeholders were identified and added to the communications management plan. What is the number of potential communication channels?

Customer requirements for the new application to be developed by an agile team limit the technology choices to only two approaches. The team members are not familiar with any of them and ask the scrum master for advice. Which of the following should the scrum master recommend to select the best approach?
option_1_content_en: A risk-based spike
option_2_content_en: Exploratory testing
option_3_content_en: An architectural spike
option_4_content_en: Prototyping

content_en: A project has short iterative planning and executing cycles where the requirements are progressively elaborated. The key stakeholders are continuously involved and provide frequent feedback allowing the team to respond to changes more quickly. What is the best way for the project manager to manage quality in this type of project environment?
option_1_content_en: By conducting periodic quality audits
option_2_content_en: By using the Validate Scope process
option_3_content_en: By scheduling regular retrospectives
option_4_content_en: By using the quality control matrix

content_en: A project manager is developing the communications management plan. She has determined which stakeholders need what information and how often she will distribute the various reports. What else should the project manager do as part of this process?
option_1_content_en: Determine the information needs of the stakeholders
option_2_content_en: Determine how the information will be transmitted
option_3_content_en: Measure the effectiveness of the communications
option_4_content_en: Submit a change request to update the communications management plan

content_en: A member of an agile project team gathered data about the project and discovered an opportunity for improvement. The team member thinks that a change to the process used by the team to develop the product of the project would improve team performance. The team member approaches the scrum master for advice on the best way to implement the change. What advice can the scrum master give to the team member?
option_1_content_en: Make the change, see what happens, then report the results during the upcoming retrospective meeting
option_2_content_en: Submit a change request, wait for the approval of the change control board, and implement the change
option_3_content_en: Send an email to the functional manager to report the findings and ask for permission to make the change
option_4_content_en: Inform the team of the opportunity for improvement and, if the team supports it, implement the change

content_en: You are a project manager conducting a meeting with your project team. The goal of the meeting is to improve the overall team environment to enhance project performance. The meeting becomes contentious with team members interrupting each other and being disrespectful to each other's suggestions. You attempt to return civility to the meeting by establishing ground rules for acceptable behavior, but working relationships may already be damaged. What might you have missed that could have prevented this situation?
option_1_content_en: Sharing the team management plan with the project team
option_2_content_en: Involving the project team in the creation of a team charter and gaining agreement with the content
option_3_content_en: Allowing the team members to work independently and avoid interaction
option_4_content_en: Making sure each team member has a copy of the project charter

content_en: You are leading a project to replace an aging bridge spanning a river in a heavily populated area. The new bridge would include a pedestrian pathway, that is not a feature of the existing bridge. The bridge is well under construction when residents learn the pathway would allow strangers to enter their neighborhood at all times. The residents demand the elimination of the pathway. What would have been the best course of action to avoid this situation?
option_1_content_en: Identify the pathway as a possible point of contention with stakeholders early in the project
option_2_content_en: Nothing could have been done differently because the project was authorized per the project charter
option_3_content_en: Engage a public relations company to handle community outreach once local residents voiced their disapproval
option_4_content_en: Reroute the pathway entrance during construction to an old railway trail instead of the local street

content_en: Your project team functions as a well-organized unit. The team members are interdependent and work through issues smoothly and effectively. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Provide clear direction on the project objectives and the behavior expected from the team members
option_2_content_en: Help the team to get through their struggle by ensuring they listen to each other and understand their differences
option_3_content_en: Ensure the team resolves conflicts quickly and continues to work collaboratively and step in only when needed
option_4_content_en: Serve as a gateway between the project team and the stakeholders and delegate decision making to the team members

content_en: A project manager is assigned to an agile software development project for a large banking corporation. With the project just getting underway, the project manager has learned about new hacking tactics that present a potential threat to regulatory compliance for the project. What should the project manager do next?
option_1_content_en: Review the risks during the project retrospective
option_2_content_en: Analyze the consequences of non-compliance
option_3_content_en: Submit a change request to update the risk management plan
option_4_content_en: Develop a cumulative flow diagram

content_en: You are preparing for an upcoming software development project. The project will be initiated and planned using a predictive approach, while the development team will use Kanban. A budget has been established for training, and you need to determine how to allocate those funds. What is your best course of action?
option_1_content_en: Send the development team to a seminar on maximizing WIP
option_2_content_en: Provide training to transform T-shaped people into I-shaped people
